images.title: Odd numbers build squares
images.purpose: Show that adding odd numbers from 1 gives the square numbers 1, 4, 9.
images.composition: Three dot squares in one row with wide gaps, one short sum label centred under each.
images.exact_structure: Three square dot grids in a row: 1 by 1 (1 dot), 2 by 2 (4 dots), 3 by 3 (9 dots), all dots the same size and evenly spaced. In each grid the newest L-shaped layer is amber #E69F00 and the older dots teal #0072B2. Counts: first grid 1 teal dot; second 1 teal and 3 amber; third 4 teal and 5 amber. One dot-count label under each grid. Exactly 3 grids.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
grids that are not exact squares, or L-layers with the wrong number of dots
images.takeaway: Adding odd numbers from 1 makes square numbers.
images.description: Three square dot grids of 1, 4 and 9 dots, each new L-shaped layer in amber, labelled 1 dot, 4 dots and 9 dots.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the amber dots in each grid and say what odd number they match.

image_decisions.why: The sums of odd numbers being squares is clearest as growing dot squares.
